h: Making a Liverpool Weekend Around the Games
p: The secret to a cracking session at a multi-activity venue is not trying to cram everything in. Pick the activities your group is most excited about, book them in advance and leave a bit of time to grab a drink or a bite in between. It's more fun when nobody is clock-watching or rushing from one thing to the next.

If you're in a big group with mixed ages, think about who's coming. Older kids and teens will love it, but some parts may have age or height rules, and evenings can be more adult-focused. Check before you book so nobody's disappointed at the door.

Liverpool city centre is packed with things to do. St George's Hall, a grand neoclassical building near Lime Street station, is a real showpiece, and the Walker Art Gallery and World Museum are close by and free to visit. The Museum of Liverpool on the waterfront tells the city's story, from its port history to its music and football.

For a different taste of Liverpool, head to Bold Street for independent cafés and restaurants serving food from all over the world, or the Baltic Triangle for creative spaces and street food. If you've got time to venture out, Crosby Beach is home to Antony Gormley's Another Place, a hundred cast-iron figures gazing out to sea.
